chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever assists his believing brother, the distressed, gasping for breath in his struggle, so he relieves his hardship and helps him succeed in his need, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him seventy-two mercies. He will hasten one of them to rectify his livelihood, and reserve seventy-one for him for the terrors and horrors of the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a distressed believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the tangible spiritual economics of *i'anat al-mu'min* (assisting the believer). The hadith uniquely quantifies the reward as seventy-two divine mercies, distinguishing between immediate worldly benefit for sustenance and eschatological protection against the fears of the Hereafter, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of dunya and akhira.
